literal: Jin's troops were greatly routed; Jin and the generals E Qing and Liu Ba were captured by Ding.
idiomatic: Jin's army was routed; Jin and his generals E Qing and Liu Ba were captured by Ding.

literal: Later when Emperor Taiwu took Pingliang, Jin and the rest were able to return.
idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Taiwu took Pingliang, Jin and the others were released and returned.

literal: He was demoted to cook and made to carry wine and food, following the imperial carriage back to the capital to shame him.
idiomatic: He was demoted to palace cook and made to carry wine and food behind the imperial carriage back to the capital as a public shame.

literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and his noble rank was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Pacifies the East and reduced to duke.

literal: At the beginning of Taiyan he was Commandant of the Guards and changed to Prince of Hengnong.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiyan he was Commandant of the Guards and made Prince of Hengnong.

literal: Later he was Grand General of Ten Thousand Cavalry.
idiomatic: He later became Grand General of Ten Thousand Cavalry.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu deliberated attacking Liangzhou, Jin and more than thirty others argued it could not be done; the emperor did not follow.
idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu deliberated attacking Liangzhou, Jin and more than thirty others argued against it; the emperor overruled them.

literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, for battle merit he was given seventy households of bond servants.
idiomatic: When Liangzhou fell, he was rewarded with seventy households of bond servants for battle merit.

literal: Also because Jin was an elder of the founding age, he was given a comfort carriage, decided prison cases, and was consulted on court government.
idiomatic: As an elder of the founding age he was also given a comfort carriage, authority to decide lawsuits, and a voice in court government.

literal: Jin was clever, argumentative, and of strong memory; skilled in discourse, when speaking at length of former-dynasty affairs, though not all were correct, he sometimes hit the mark, and listeners sighed and praised.
idiomatic: Clever, argumentative, and retentive, Jin was skilled in discourse; recounting former-dynasty affairs he did not always get things right, yet often struck home, and listeners marveled.

literal: Whenever great government was deliberated, his views were often followed; the court praised him.
idiomatic: Whenever great affairs of state were debated, his counsel was often followed, and the court praised him.

literal: In the ninth year of Zhenjun he died, aged eighty-nine.
idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenjun he died at eighty-nine.

literal: Emperor Taiwu personally came to mourn in grief, posthumous title Zhao.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu came in person to mourn him deeply and gave him the posthumous title Zhao.

literal: Jin had several tens of wives and more than twenty sons.
idiomatic: Jin had several dozen wives and more than twenty sons.

literal: His eldest son Taguan inherited the fief.
idiomatic: His eldest son Taguan inherited the fief.

literal: Emperor Taiwu said: "Jin's defeat in the western expedition carries the state's regular penalty.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu said, "Jin's defeat on the western expedition carried the state's regular penalty."

literal: Because he aided the Mandate in the former dynasty, his rank and office were restored, intending to reap the effect of Meng Ming.
idiomatic: "Because he aided the Mandate under the former emperor, his rank and office were restored, intending to reap the redemption of Meng Ming."

literal: Now Jin has ended his natural years—the distinction of ruler and minister is complete.
idiomatic: "Now Jin has ended his natural span, and the distinction of ruler and minister stands complete."

literal: Thereupon Taguan's rank was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: Taguan's title was thereupon reduced to duke.

literal: The fief passed to his grandson Xu; he had no son and the state was abolished.
idiomatic: The fief passed to his grandson Xu; Xu had no heir and the line was abolished.

literal: In the Taihe era Emperor Xiaowen posthumously recorded the meritorious ministers of the former dynasty and granted Jin a share in the temple sacrifices.
idiomatic: In the Taihe era Emperor Xiaowen recorded the meritorious ministers of former reigns and granted Jin a share in the temple sacrifices.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu continued an extinguished line, making Xu's nephew Jian heir to continue the descent.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu continued the extinguished line by making Xu's nephew Jian heir to the house.

literal: Shu Sun Jian was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Shu Sun Jian was a man of Dai.

literal: His father Gu was reared by Empress Dowager Wang, mother of Emperor Zhaocheng, and ranked with the princes.
idiomatic: His father Gu was reared by Empress Dowager Wang, mother of Emperor Zhaocheng, and ranked with the imperial sons.

literal: Jian in youth was famed for penetrating intelligence.
idiomatic: Jian was famed from youth for penetrating intelligence.

literal: When Emperor Daowu visited the Helan tribe he constantly followed at left and right.
idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu visited the Helan tribe he constantly attended him.

literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he was Outer Court Grandee; with An Tong and twelve others he took turns managing common affairs and took part in the state's stratagems.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he was Outer Court Grandee; with An Tong and twelve others he took turns managing routine affairs and advised on state strategy.

literal: He followed Prince of Qin Gu as envoy to Murong Chui; six years passed before he returned.
idiomatic: He followed Prince of Qin Gu as envoy to Murong Chui and was away six years before returning.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Central Camp Commander, enfeoffed as Duke of Ping'an, and sent out as Inspector of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: He rose to Central Camp Commander, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ping'an, and sent out as Inspector of Bingzhou.

literal: Later he was dismissed for a public matter and guarded the Ye city gardens.
idiomatic: He was later dismissed over a public matter and guarded the Ye city gardens.

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, remembering former merit, he was made General of Uprightness and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, remembering his former service, he was made General of Uprightness and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

literal: Starving Hu Liu Wu and others gathered factions and rebelled.
idiomatic: Starving Hu led by Liu Wu gathered factions and rebelled.

literal: Emperor Mingyuan lent Jian his former title and Duke of Ping'an and ordered Gongsun Biao and others to attack Wu.
idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan restored Jian's former title as Duke of Ping'an and ordered Gongsun Biao and others to attack Wu.

literal: More than ten thousand heads were cut off; the rest fled in panic, threw themselves into the Zhi River and drowned—the water ceased to flow.
idiomatic: More than ten thousand heads were taken; the rest fled into the Zhi River and drowned until the water ceased to flow.

literal: The Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong and ordered his subordinate Wang Zhongde as vanguard to press on Huatai.
idiomatic: Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong and sent his subordinate Wang Zhongde as vanguard against Huatai.

literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Wei Jian led his command and abandoned the city to cross the river.
idiomatic: Inspector of Yanzhou Wei Jian led his forces to abandon the city and cross the river.

literal: Zhongde thereupon entered Huatai and proclaimed: "Jin's original intent was to borrow passage with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk from Wei—not expecting Wei's garrison commander to abandon the city so readily.
idiomatic: Zhongde entered Huatai and proclaimed, "Jin meant only to borrow passage with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk from Wei—not expecting Wei's commander to abandon the city at once."

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan heard, he ordered Jian to cross the river and display might, executed Wei Jian, and cast his corpse into the river.
idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan heard, he ordered Jian to cross the river and display Wei power, executed Wei Jian, and cast his corpse into the river.

literal: He called Zhongde's soldiers to speak and questioned them on the offense of invading the borders.
idiomatic: He summoned Zhongde's soldiers, questioned them, and rebuked their border violation.

literal: Soon he was transferred to garrison commander of Guang'a; his martial name was very renowned.
idiomatic: He was soon transferred to garrison commander of Guang'a, where his martial renown was great.

literal: After long service he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, General of Chu Troops, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: After long service he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, General of Chu Troops, and Inspector of Xuzhou.

literal: He led troops across the river from Pingyuan and swept down the commanderies of Qing and Yan.
idiomatic: He led troops across the river from Pingyuan and swept the commanderies of Qing and Yan.

literal: He then entered Qingzhou eastward and besieged Song Inspector Zhu Kui at Dongyang city.
idiomatic: He then entered Qingzhou and besieged Song inspector Zhu Kui at Dongyang.

literal: Song sent the generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde to rescue Kui; Jian could not take the city and withdrew.
idiomatic: Song sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde to relieve Kui; Jian failed to take the city and withdrew.

literal: For merit he was given the fief of Duke of Shouguang.
idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shouguang.

literal: With Duke of Ruyin Changsun Daosheng he crossed the river south; Zhongde and the rest from Qing entered Ji eastward and fled toward Qingzhou.
idiomatic: With Duke of Ruyin Changsun Daosheng he crossed south; Zhongde and others entered Ji from Qing and fled east toward Qingzhou.

literal: Emperor Taiwu, because Jian's martial name shook the south and Song feared him, made him Grand General of the Pingyuan Garrison, enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang, and added General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, because Jian's name shook the south and Song feared him, made him Grand General of the Pingyuan Garrison, Prince of Danyang, and General Who Pacifies the South.

literal: Earlier, frontier troops south of You and Yi were gathered on the river—one route to attack Luoyang, one to attack Huatai.
idiomatic: Earlier, frontier troops south of You and Yi had been gathered on the river—one column to strike Luoyang, one Huatai.

literal: Song generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde rescued Huatai.
idiomatic: Song generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde marched to relieve Huatai.

literal: Jian and Duke of Ruyin Daosheng resisted and struck them.
idiomatic: Jian and Duke of Ruyin Daosheng met and repulsed them.

literal: Jian divided the army for flanking battle, sent light cavalry to intercept front and rear, and burned grain and fodder to cut their supply route.
idiomatic: Jian divided his forces for flanking attacks, sent light cavalry to harry front and rear, and burned grain and fodder to sever their supply line.

literal: Daoji's troops were hungry; deserters followed one after another.
idiomatic: Daoji's army starved; deserters followed one after another.

literal: By this An Gu and the rest were able to lift the siege of Huatai.
idiomatic: Thus An Gu and the others were able to lift the siege of Huatai.

literal: Jian was deep, keen, and full of stratagems; in eastern and western campaigns he was constantly chief planner; his bearing was clear and ordered, and he was styled Severe and Bright.
idiomatic: Deep, keen, and full of stratagems, Jian was constantly chief planner in eastern and western campaigns; clear in bearing, he was styled Severe and Bright.

literal: He also elegantly valued human relations, honored the worthy, and loved scholars.
idiomatic: He also valued human relations, honored the worthy, and loved scholars.

literal: At Pingyuan for more than ten years he soothed within and without and won great border praise.
idiomatic: At Pingyuan for more than ten years he soothed subjects within and without and won high praise on the frontier.

literal: Among the famed generals at the beginning of Wei, few could match him.
idiomatic: Among Wei's early famed generals, few could match him.

literal: The south feared his martial stratagems; Qing and Yan for long ceased raiding.
idiomatic: The south feared his stratagems, and Qing and Yan long ceased their raids.

literal: In the third year of Taiyan he died, aged seventy-three; posthumous title Xiang, burial granted at Jinling.
idiomatic: In the third year of Taiyan he died at seventy-three with the posthumous title Xiang and burial at Jinling.

literal: Earlier, when Jun died, Emperor Mingyuan told his wife Lady Huan: "In life you shared glory together; in death you should share one tomb—whoever can follow in burial may do as she wishes.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Jun died, Emperor Mingyuan told his wife Lady Huan, "In life you shared glory; in death you should share one tomb—whoever will follow him in burial may choose freely."

literal: Lady Huan thereupon strangled herself and they were buried together.
idiomatic: Lady Huan strangled herself and they were buried together.

literal: Since Jun had been Duke of Ancheng, Jun's younger brother Lin inherited their father's fief, was reduced to Duke of Danyang, and held Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand General of the Liangzhou Garrison.
idiomatic: Jun having been Duke of Ancheng, his younger brother Lin inherited their father's fief, was reduced to Duke of Danyang, and served as Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand General of the Liangzhou Garrison.

literal: With the garrison deputy Xi Mu, both as noble kinsmen's sons, they vied in greed for wealth and goods, then denounced each other, and were executed for the offense.
idiomatic: He and garrison deputy Xi Mu, both noble kinsmen, vied in greed for wealth, denounced each other, and were executed.

literal: An Tong was a man of the Hu of Liaodong.
idiomatic: An Tong was a man of the Hu of Liaodong.

literal: His remote ancestor was called Shigao; in Han times he entered Luoyang as the attendant son of the King of Parthia.
idiomatic: His remote ancestor Shigao entered Luoyang in Han times as the attendant son of the King of Parthia.

literal: Through Wei to Jin, fleeing turmoil he went to Liaodong and there made his home.
idiomatic: Through Wei and Jin, fleeing turmoil, he settled in Liaodong.

literal: His father Qu served Murong Yong.
idiomatic: His father Qu served Murong Yong.

literal: When Yong was destroyed by Fu Jian, Qu's friend Gongsun Juan's younger sister was taken into the Fu clan palace and later given out to Liu Kuren as wife; Kuren favored and cherished her.
idiomatic: When Yong fell to Fu Jian, Qu's friend Gongsun Juan's younger sister was taken into Fu Jian's palace and later given to Liu Kuren as wife; Kuren favored her deeply.

literal: Tong followed Juan in trade; seeing that Emperor Daowu had talent to save the age, he remained to serve.
idiomatic: Tong followed Juan in trade, saw in Emperor Daowu the talent to save the age, and remained to serve him.

literal: His nature was upright, severe, bright, and discerning; he loved the words of elders.
idiomatic: Upright, severe, bright, and discerning, he loved the counsel of elders.

literal: At the beginning of Dengguo Emperor Daowu raised troops from Murong Chui; Tong repeatedly went as envoy and pleased the intent.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo, when Emperor Daowu raised troops from Murong Chui, Tong repeatedly went as envoy and pleased him.

literal: He was Outer Court Grandee; with He Ba and others he entered and left within the forbidden precincts, taking turns managing common affairs.
idiomatic: He was Outer Court Grandee; with He Ba and others he moved within the forbidden precincts, taking turns managing routine affairs.

literal: Following the campaign against Yao Ping at Chaibi, when Yao Xing mustered all his forces to rescue Ping, Tong advanced a plan: "East of the Fen there is Meng Pit, more than three hundred li east to west, with no path through.
idiomatic: Campaigning against Yao Ping at Chaibi, when Yao Xing mustered all his forces to rescue Ping, Tong proposed, "East of the Fen lies Meng Pit, more than three hundred li across with no path through."

literal: When Yao Xing comes he is sure to come by the west of the Fen, taking the high ground to look down, going straight to Chaibi—thus the enemy within and without will join their strength.
idiomatic: "When Yao Xing comes he will surely take the west bank, hold the high ground, and strike straight for Chaibi—then enemy within and without will join strength."

literal: We should cut the Fen into north and south floating bridges and build a rampart on the west bank.
idiomatic: "Cut the Fen with north and south floating bridges and build a rampart on the west bank."

literal: Once the western rampart is firm, when the enemy arrives he will have nowhere to deploy his stratagems.
idiomatic: "Once the western rampart stands firm, the enemy will have nowhere to deploy his stratagems."

literal: They followed this.
idiomatic: They followed his plan.

literal: Xing indeed watched Ping slaughtered and could not save him.
idiomatic: Xing indeed watched Ping destroyed and could not save him.

literal: For stratagem merit he was given the fief of Marquis of Beixin.
idiomatic: For this stratagem he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Beixin.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu supervised the state and held court to hear government, Tong was made Left Assistant.
idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu supervised the state and held court, Tong was made Left Assistant.

literal: At his accession his rank was advanced to Duke of Gaoyang and he held the two provinces Ji and Qing.
idiomatic: At his accession Tong was advanced to Duke of Gaoyang and governed Ji and Qing.

literal: Tong's eldest son Qu, under Emperor Mingyuan, managed Imperial Granary affairs; he stole several piculs of official husked rice, intending to support his parents.
idiomatic: Tong's eldest son Qu, under Emperor Mingyuan, managed the Imperial Granary; he stole several piculs of official rice to support his parents.

literal: Tong was greatly angry, asked to execute Qu, and impeached himself for failing to instruct his son.
idiomatic: Tong was furious, asked to execute Qu, and impeached himself for failing to instruct his son.

literal: The emperor praised this and pardoned him; thereupon an edict long supplied rice.
idiomatic: The emperor praised his integrity and pardoned Qu, then ordered rice supplied in perpetuity.

literal: Tong in office was bright in perception and skilled at auditing; his household rules were strict and ordered, and he was praised by the age.
idiomatic: In office Tong was bright in perception and skilled at audit; his household rules were strict, and the age praised him.

literal: When he was in Jizhou, old in years, he greatly accumulated wealth and goods and raised temple towers on a grand scale, to the suffering of the common people.
idiomatic: In Jizhou, old in years, he amassed wealth and raised temple towers on a grand scale, to the people's suffering.

literal: He died; posthumously made Prince of Gaoyang, posthumous title Gonghui.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Prince of Gaoyang with the posthumous title Gonghui.

literal: Qu's younger brother Yuan had an elegant nature, stern and reserved, deep courage, and many stratagems.
idiomatic: Qu's younger brother Yuan was elegant, stern, reserved, deeply courageous, and full of stratagems.

literal: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was Hunt Officer and went out to supervise Yunzhong military affairs.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was Hunt Officer and supervised Yunzhong military affairs.

literal: At that time Helian Qubuqin invaded Hexi; Yuan with several tens of horsemen struck him and killed more than ten men.
idiomatic: When Helian Qubuqin invaded Hexi, Yuan with several dozen horsemen struck him and killed more than ten of his men.

literal: The emperor, because Yuan treated the enemy lightly and violated command, added punishment.
idiomatic: The emperor punished him for treating the enemy lightly and violating command.

literal: Yet knowing Yuan was fierce and brave, he then entrusted him as general and garrisoned Yunzhong.
idiomatic: Yet knowing Yuan's fierceness, he then entrusted him as general at Yunzhong.

literal: When the Rouran invaded the frontier, Yuan repeatedly broke them; for merit he was given Marquis of Wuyuan and made General of Lu Troops.
idiomatic: When the Rouran invaded the frontier Yuan repeatedly routed them and, for merit, was made Marquis of Wuyuan and General of Lu Troops.

literal: His younger brother Yan was eloquent, discerning, and full of strategy, most having his father's manner.
idiomatic: His younger brother Yan was eloquent, discerning, and strategic, most in his father's manner.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mingyuan he was Chief Inner Attendant and ordered to inspect and recommend the hundred offices, impeaching wickedness, sparing none.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Mingyuan he was Chief Inner Attendant, ordered to inspect the hundred offices and impeach wickedness without sparing anyone.

literal: He once reported his father's private affairs; the emperor considered this loyal and especially favored him.
idiomatic: He once reported his father's private misconduct; the emperor deemed this loyalty and favored him especially.

literal: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin from Chang'an pursued Helian Chang to Anding, Yan was Supervising Army Attendant Censor.
idiomatic: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin pursued Helian Chang from Chang'an to Anding, Yan was Supervising Army Attendant Censor.

literal: Jin, because many horses died of plague and the soldiers lacked grain, fortified deeply and held firm.
idiomatic: Jin, with plague killing many horses and grain running short, fortified deeply and held firm.

literal: He sent the Grand Master of the Stud Qiu Dui and others to supervise tax grain among the people; they were defeated by Chang.
idiomatic: He sent Grand Master of the Stud Qiu Dui and others to levy grain among the people; Chang defeated them.

literal: Chang thereupon grew arrogant and proud, coming daily to raid and plunder.
idiomatic: Chang then grew arrogant and came daily to raid and plunder.
